title: Prawn Thermidor
subtitle: Prawns in a rich mustard and cream sauce, grilled with cheese
excerpt: King prawns in a rich, mustardy cream sauce flavoured with tarragon and brandy, spooned back into the shells and grilled under a cheese crust. An indulgent main course or dinner party starter.

recipe.sourceNotes: Thermidor is a classic French sauce associated primarily with Lobster Thermidor, one of the great French restaurant dishes, named after the month of Thermidor in the French Revolutionary calendar. The original Lobster Thermidor is attributed to the Parisian restaurant Chez Marie on the opening night of the play Thermidor in January 1894. The sauce — a reduction of white wine, shallots, and tarragon finished with cream, Dijon mustard, and brandy — is rich, intensely savoury, and works with any shellfish. This version uses king prawns as an accessible and more economical alternative to lobster while preserving the essential character of the dish. The gratin finish under the grill provides the characteristic browned cheese crust.

recipeTools.notes: A frying pan for the sauce. A baking tray for the grill finish.

content.text: Butterfly the prawns from the back to open them out: use a sharp knife to cut along the back of each prawn through the shell without cutting all the way through, then open the prawn out flat. This creates a larger surface area for the sauce and allows the prawns to sit stably in the dish during grilling. Do not overcook the prawns: they are cooked initially in butter, then finished under the grill. The second period of heat is brief; the prawns should be cooked through but still juicy.

items.preparation: large raw king prawns, shell-on; butterflied from the back
finely grated; for the gratin crust

content.text: Heat the butter in a frying pan over high heat. Sear the prawns for 1 to 2 minutes per side until just pink. Remove and arrange on a baking tray. In the same pan over medium heat, fry the shallot and garlic for 3 minutes. Add the brandy and let it bubble. Add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the cream and simmer for 3 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the Dijon mustard, tarragon, salt, and cayenne. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Spoon the sauce generously over each prawn. Scatter the Parmesan over the top. Grill under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling. Serve immediately with lemon wedges and crusty bread or rice.
